I will keep the land in the wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou, this is the cropping pattern I trust most because it fits the local water, temperature, and machinery conditions, and at my age I want steady output more than risk. I will finish the winter wheat already in the field, then follow it with summer maize on the same land. I will use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize because I want stable emergence, better lodging resistance, and reliable yield. I will not spread myself into cotton, vegetables, or other crops because they take more labor, more management, and usually more market risk than I want to carry.

For management, I will keep things simple and practical. I will use rotary tillage because it matches local machine work and is easier for me to handle than deep ploughing every season. On wheat, I will focus fertilizer on enough nitrogen for tillering and grain fill, with moderate phosphorus and potassium, and I will irrigate at the key times so I do not waste water. After wheat harvest, I will sow maize quickly to catch heat and moisture, use a little heavier nitrogen than wheat, and keep two irrigations ready if rainfall is not enough. I will spray only when needed, mainly to control the common diseases, weeds, and insects that can cut yield. My goal is not to chase the very highest yield; it is to keep the work manageable, the cost controlled, and the harvest dependable.
